overall_assessment: Anonymization works well at uis. None of the 28 sampled plans has personal data left, and full-text scans of all 2728 plans find no e-mail, role+name, '(Role)' staff line or name-only line outside reading lists. All three staff-list layouts (HTML 'Fagperson(er)', PDF 'Fagpersoner'/'Fagpersonar' blocks, including roles such as 'Hovedansvarlig'), version stamps, PDF page footers and OpenURL links with user_ip are removed, and the earlier 'Studiepoeng 15 Emneansvarlig <name>' leak is fixed. Every pre-pass flag is a false alarm (see findings[0] for the one real defect): phone matches ID numbers in URLs (proquest docview, HUL repository, NRK), name_label matches 'Teacher' in article titles, name_like matches reference authors, admin_date matches newspaper publication dates ('7. juni, 2021') that should stay, and removed counts OpenURL resolver links (removed by design, #287) and staff lists. The only defect is that generic date rules strip dates and titles from reading lists: 170 removals in 134 of 2728 plans.

findings.evidence: Utdanningsdirektoratets spørreundersøkelse til lærere [−høsten 2020−] Karl Solbue Vika
findings.description: Generic admin-date rules remove dates that belong to literature references, which the rubric says to keep (publication years, titles, dates of what directorates publish). Visible in the packet: the season-year rule deletes 'høsten 2020' from the title of the NIFU/Udir report 'Spørsmål til Skole-Norge høsten 2020: Analyser og resultater fra Utdanningsdirektoratets spørreundersøkelse til lærere'. This hits all 4 sampled MGLT43-1 plans and 11 plans institution-wide. Checks on the full plans find the same kind of loss in three more rules, all in parts of the plans that the packet cuts off. (1) The dd.mm.yyyy rule removes publication dates of media references in 52 plans. In MGL2050-1/MGL1050-1 2021, 'Martine Rauken, 19.10.2021,' becomes 'Martine Rauken, ,', while 'Mae Ngai, 21. april 2021,' in the same list stays. (2) .drop_academic_year reads ISO year-month dates as academic years 50 times: in LHIS175-1 2022, '2, 95, 2008-09, 452-491' becomes '2, 95, , 452-491', and elsewhere '2001-02-01' becomes '-01'. It also removes content year ranges: Helsedirektoratet's 'Norkost 3 … 2010-2011' survey in about 20 MGL1090/2090 plans, and the Storting session years of Riksrevisjonen 'Dokument 3:6 (2020-2021)', leaving '3:6:'. (3) The slash rule removes years in 9 plans ('Spillerom 1992/1993'). In total: 170 removals in 134 of 2728 plans. These are small losses of reference metadata, sometimes leaving stray commas; course content outside the reading lists is not affected.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(). (a) In the season-year rule, the .not_gov lookbehind sits at the end of the match, and its window [^\n]{0,80} cannot cross the PDF line break inside 'høsten\n2020'. So 'Utdanningsdirektoratets', which is on the same line as 'høsten', is not seen. (b) The season-year, dd.mm.yyyy and academic-year rules run over the whole plan, including the 'Litteratur' reading list. .drop_academic_year cannot tell '2008-09' (September 2008) from an academic year. .gov_doc_regex does not know 'Dokument N:N' or 'Riksrevisjonen'.
findings.suggested_fix: (a) In .anon_generic(), put the guard before the match: paste0(.not_gov, "\\b(?i:", .season_regex, ")\\s*\\d{4}\\b"), and do the same for the dd.mm.yyyy and range rules. Alternatively, widen the window in .not_gov to cross one line break ("(?:[^\\n]|\\n(?!\\n)){0,80}"). (b) Split the text at the first '(?m)^Litteratur\\s*$' line. In the tail, apply only the personal-data rules (e-mail, staff lines, role+name, OpenURL, user_ip, phone), not the season-year, dd.mm.yyyy, academic-year or clock rules. Also add '[Dd]okument[ \\t]?\\d+:\\d+|riksrevisjon' to .gov_doc_regex. Tests for tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R: 'Utdanningsdirektoratets spørreundersøkelse til lærere høsten\n2020' is kept; under 'Litteratur', '2, 95, 2008-09, 452-491' and 'Martine Rauken, 19.10.2021,' are kept; 'Dette er studietilbudet for studieår 2025-2026.' still loses its year. This changes what the data mean, so it needs a methods.qmd entry and an explanation in metrics_check.
